paper.title: Lotka-Volterra predator-prey dynamics (agent-based; NetLogo wolf-sheep-grass realisation)
paper.journal: Lotka 1925, Elements of Physical Biology; Volterra 1926, Nature 118:558-560

headline: Agent Lotka-Volterra (wolf-sheep-grass): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; survival 100% (10/10 seeds), predator lags prey (median cross-corr lag = +119 ticks)

verdicts.gate: P1 sustained oscillations, no extinction: both species >=2 peaks AND neither extinct in >=60% of seeds
P2 predator lags prey: cross-correlation(prey, predator) peaks at a POSITIVE lag (majority of surviving seeds; positive median lag)
P3 persistence: oscillation continues into the last third (both species peak there) in >=60% of surviving seeds

extra.locked_metric: prey/predator population series; survival; cross-corr lag
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of the classic Lotka-Volterra result via its standard agent-based (NetLogo wolf-sheep-grass) realisation; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce sustained oscillations with the predator lagging the prey, and report the extinction-proneness honestly. The grass resource supplies the carrying-capacity term that lets the discrete stochastic system settle onto a sustained cycle rather than diverging or collapsing.

citations: Lotka, A.J. (1925). Elements of Physical Biology. Williams & Wilkins.
Volterra, V. (1926). Fluctuations in the abundance of a species considered mathematically. Nature 118:558-560. doi:10.1038/118558a0.
Wilensky, U. (1997). NetLogo Wolf Sheep Predation model. Center for Connected Learning and Computer-Based Modeling, Northwestern University. (the standard agent-based realisation reproduced here.)

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded on the prey/predator population series (survival, peaks, predator-lags-prey cross-correlation)
